newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan welcomes Hebron deal as "fresh beginning".
newsitem.headline: Jordan welcomes Hebron deal as "fresh beginning".

text.p: Jordan welcomed on Wednesday a deal on Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron, clinched after a last-ditch intervention by King Hussein.
"We are very happy about this agreement," Information Minister Marwan Muasher told Reuters. "We are very hopeful that we have a fresh beginning now that will lead us to comprehensive peace."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat sealed the U.S.-brokered accord at a late-night summit and agreed on a timeframe for further Israeli pullbacks in the West Bank.
Negotiations had stalled before King Hussein flew to Gaza and Tel Aviv on Sunday for talks with Arafat and Netanyahu.

"We feel that it is a culmination of concerted efforts made by different parties over the last few months. In particular the Egyptians and the Americans have been very helpful in getting us to this point," Muasher said.

"Jordan, under the leadership of King Hussein, made use of its very good relations with all the parties in the region to bridge the gap to restore some of the lost trust between the parties which made this effort possible," he added.

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was due to be given self-rule 10 months ago but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.

"The peace process has taken a new course from this point on -- a course that would lead us to full implementation of the Oslo accord and to successful negotiation over the final status of the West Bank and Gaza," Muasher said.
